purpose: Stop the phase 3 maintenance detector from pausing the entire system because a user-submitted post title on a healthy board contained the substring 점검.
design_intent: Phase 3 built a competent Korean datetime parser and wired it to a trigger with no corroboration requirement. A bare keyword hit is sufficient - HTTP 200 with a full board of rows still trips it. The observer already holds the disambiguating signal (rowCount) and does not use it. The fix is not a better keyword list; it is requiring the page to actually look unavailable before believing text that says it is.
prerequisite: None strictly - R4 is independent of R1-R3 and may be pulled forward if a false-positive pause is observed in production.

model_execution_guidance.recommended_model: Deep reasoning model for MC-001 and MC-002; a fast model is adequate for MC-004 once the fixture exists
model_execution_guidance.note: Capture the real board fixture before changing the detector. Without a realistic HTTP-200 fixture the change cannot be shown to work, and the existing maintenanceNotice.test.ts only exercises the true-positive direction.

work_items.title: Require corroboration before declaring maintenance
work_items.action: parseMaintenanceNotice gains a required `signals` argument carrying rowCount and writeButtonCount. Replace the trigger at L82 with: maintenance = statusCode in {502,503,504} OR (keyword AND rowCount === 0 AND writeButtonCount === 0). getBoardDiagnostics already computes both counts and can pass them through. Every existing caller must be updated; the argument is required rather than optional so a missed call site is a compile error, not a silent revert to the old behaviour.
work_items.rationale: The keyword list includes the unanchored substring 점검중 (L45), scanned against page.innerText('body') of a deals board carrying roughly twenty user-submitted post titles. On Ppomppu, 점검 (inspection) is ordinary commercial vocabulary.

work_items.title: Scope the time-range parse to the matched notice line
work_items.action: Both date-range regexes currently run against the whole textCombined. Once isMaintenance is true, timeRangeRegex (L144) matches any HH:MM ~ HH:MM or N시 ~ M시 anywhere on the page, and board rows and deal titles are full of times. Run the parse against the matched notice line (already computed as noticeSnippet) plus a small window of surrounding lines, not the entire body.

work_items.title: Cap the parsed maintenance window
work_items.action: A single unlucky match can currently set maintenanceBlockedUntil up to roughly 24 hours out, and that value is persisted to disk and survives restart. Cap the parsed window at a defensible maximum - 6 hours suggested. Anything longer falls back to the 30-minute default and logs a warning carrying the raw notice text, so a real long maintenance window is visible to the operator rather than silently applied.

work_items.title: Add the false-positive regression fixture
work_items.action: Capture a realistic HTTP-200 Ppomppu board page whose post titles contain 점검 and at least one HH:MM ~ HH:MM string. Assert isMaintenance === false. This fixture is the regression guard and is worth taking from a real board page rather than hand-writing, because the failure mode is precisely that hand-written fixtures are too clean. Keep the existing true-positive tests passing unchanged.

work_items.title: Replace string-sniffed control flow for the maintenance decision
work_items.action: The publisher currently detects platform maintenance by testing `log.error?.includes('PLATFORM_MAINTENANCE')`. Carry the condition as a structured field on the observer result rather than as a substring of a human-readable error message. Low urgency but cheap while this file is open, and the string coupling will break the first time the message is reworded.

acceptance_criteria: A healthy HTTP-200 board fixture containing 점검 in a post title and a time range in another yields isMaintenance === false.
An HTTP 503 response yields isMaintenance === true regardless of body text.
A genuine maintenance page (keyword, zero rows, no write button) yields isMaintenance === true with the correct parsed window.
No parsed maintenance window exceeds the cap; one that would produces a warning log carrying the raw notice.
The publisher's maintenance branch is selected by a structured field, not a substring match.
out_of_scope: Scheduler behaviour once maintenance is detected - that path is correct and R1's clamp already protects it.
Expanding the keyword list. The defect is the trigger condition, not keyword coverage.

gate_criteria: npm run lint:structure passes with 0 errors
npm run lint passes with 0 errors
npm run test:unit passes, including the new false-positive fixture and all pre-existing true-positive cases
